key_insight: Halide substitution in Ca$_3$PX$_3$ strongly tunes stability, bandgap, and solar efficiency, with Ca$_3$PI$_3$ emerging as the best photovoltaic candidate.
engineering_relevance: This suggests composition engineering can optimize perovskite-like absorbers for higher-efficiency solar cell design without changing the overall crystal family.
method: First-principles structural and electronic property analysis
Band structure and optical parameter evaluation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct bandgaps from 2.0 to 3.788 eV and SLME results up to 29.6% for Ca$_3$PI$_3$, while Ca$_3$PF$_3$ is only 0.6%.
watch_item: These are theoretical screening results, so experimental synthesis, stability, and device-level losses still need validation before deployment.
paper_title: Halide substitution effects on the photovoltaic properties of Ca$_3$PX$_3$ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) perovskites: advancing solar cell efficiency
